cells.name: Continuity and responsiveness
cells.example: T4, T5, T6 each name and answer the previous mind's claim.
cells.limitation: T7 ignores T6's decay claim; T10 leaves T8's cost objection unanswered.

cells.name: Development of ideas
cells.example: T7 adds a non-initiation test; T8 adds its cost to the lovely meetings.
cells.limitation: No new distinction after T3 is introduced and then used by a later turn.

cells.name: Exploration of central tensions
cells.example: T5 vs T6: scorekeeping breeds resentment versus friendship as exchange.
cells.limitation: Friend's possible reasons and the risk of actually saying something never examined.

cells.name: Integration of perspectives
cells.example: T9 Reciprocity Theorist adopts T5's resentment point.
cells.limitation: T9 abandons Mauss wholesale without answering its own T6 rebuttal; capitulation, not reshaping.

cells.name: Progress toward understanding
cells.example: T10 narrows dispute to meeting quality versus balanced effort.
cells.limitation: T10 and section D restate the opening divide; the speak-up question stays undeveloped.

cells.name: Faithful engagement
cells.example: T5 fairly restates T4's case for speaking up before challenging it.
cells.limitation: T8 recasts a two-week pause as withdrawing presence entirely.

cells.name: Substance of challenges
cells.example: T8 names a concrete cost of T7's test: loss of lovely time.
cells.limitation: Objections in T4-T6 assert rather than name assumptions; targets rarely answer them.

cells.name: Accuracy and support
cells.example: T3 and T6 render Mauss's gift and counter-gift faithfully.
cells.limitation: T7 silent-test advice sits oddly with Attached's direct-communication stance; romantic book stretched to friendship.

cells.name: Calibration and transparency
cells.example: Section A marks the friend's indifference versus passivity as unknown.
cells.limitation: T4 asserts the user's insecurity; T1 calls communication the only way.

cells.name: Intellectual honesty and revision
cells.example: T9 concedes and names T5's resentment point as cause.
cells.limitation: T7 drops T1's communication-only stance with no cause; T8 objection never answered.

cells.name: Identification of the actual concern
cells.example: Section A frames indifferent versus simply passive friend.
cells.limitation: The asked question, whether and how to say something, drifts to accept-or-test by T7.

cells.name: Meaningful use of personal context
cells.example: T8 and section E use the lovely meetings as a cost.
cells.limitation: T7 test repeats what the user already observed: when they stop texting, nothing happens.

cells.name: Fit with goals and values
cells.example: Section E branches on whether user values time together or mutual effort.
cells.limitation: T1 imputes unmet attachment needs the user never stated as goals.

cells.name: Attention to constraints and stakes
cells.example: T8 weighs losing enjoyable time against testing the friend.
cells.limitation: T1 and T4 invent anxiety and insecurity; friendship history and length never considered.

cells.name: Responsiveness to information
cells.example: Section E branches on the user's priority between quality and equality.
cells.limitation: Never asks whether friend ever initiated, accepts every invite, or why they might not.

cells.name: Clarification of desires and motivations
cells.example: Section D offers validation or companionship as alternative motives.
cells.limitation: Validation framed pejoratively; T1 asserts unmet connection needs rather than offering alternatives.

cells.name: Examination of assumptions
cells.example: T2 surfaces placing one's peace in the friend's hands.
cells.limitation: Assumption that initiating equals caring is never opened to reflection.

cells.name: Clarification of values and priorities
cells.example: T10 names meeting quality versus balanced social dynamic as the conflict.
cells.limitation: Values posed as a binary in T10 and E; a both-and option unexplored.

cells.name: Recognition of fears and outside expectations
cells.example: T5 names resentment as a risk of scorekeeping.
cells.limitation: T1 and T4 lean on anxiety and insecurity; fear of seeming needy never named.

cells.name: Agency and reflective ownership
cells.example: Section E offers conditional branches the user can weigh.
cells.limitation: T2 issues a verdict: placing peace in their hands is a mistake.

cells.name: Definition of the decision and options
cells.example: Speak up (T1), accept (T9), pause initiating (T7) are all present.
cells.limitation: Saying something is never specified: what to say, how lightly, when.

cells.name: Explanation of tradeoffs
cells.example: T8 costs the test; E costs acceptance as continued planning frustration.
cells.limitation: The cost or risk of raising it with the friend is never weighed.

cells.name: Identification of decisive conditions
cells.example: Section E: if friend's interest unknown, a non-initiation period observes it.
cells.limitation: T7 two weeks not drawn from user's facts; E conditions are inner values, not observables.

cells.name: Treatment of uncertainty
cells.example: Section A and E isolate the friend's level of interest as key unknown.
cells.limitation: Other unknowns, the friend's reasons or habits, never separated from minor ones.

cells.name: Proportionate next steps
cells.example: T7 proposes a period of non-initiation as a low-conflict step.
cells.limitation: Step duplicates what user already knows and T8's objection to it stands unanswered.

cells.name: Accessible language
cells.example: T5 plain phrasing: not truly giving, but trading.
cells.limitation: T6 abstract: social structure of the friendship might be decaying.

cells.name: Traceable arguments and references
cells.example: T9 names the Stoic Realist and the resentment point it adopts.
cells.limitation: T7 does not say which earlier claim its test responds to.

cells.name: Manageable pacing and turn length
cells.example: Ten turns, all within the word range per checks.
cells.limitation: Near-identical turn lengths give a flat cadence across T1-T10.

cells.name: Distinguishable positions and voices
cells.example: Three titled minds with distinct stances: communicate, detach, reciprocate.
cells.limitation: One shared hedged register; Stoic in T2 lacks any Aurelian voice.

cells.name: Economy and sustained attention
cells.example: Turns stay short and on topic throughout.
cells.limitation: T4, T5, T6 open by restating the prior claim; T10 recaps.

cells.name: Meaningful stakes and tension
cells.example: T8 sets the lovely meetings at risk against the test.
cells.limitation: Stakes stay abstract; the friend never becomes a concrete presence.

cells.name: Surprise and reversals
cells.example: T9 drops its exchange claim, naming T5's resentment point.
cells.limitation: T9 ignores its own T6 rebuttal; T7 reverses T1 with no stated cause.

cells.name: Personality and expressive voice
cells.example: T5 Stoic: you are not truly giving, but trading.
cells.limitation: Minds speak in one advisory register: you should, you might.

cells.name: Memorable delivery
cells.example: T6: a gift never returned eventually stops being a gift.
cells.limitation: No analogy or concrete scene beyond those two lines.

cells.name: Anticipation and emotional movement
cells.example: T7 test proposal briefly shifts the debate toward action.
cells.limitation: Uniform rhythm and intensity from T1 to T10; no build or release.

strengths: T5 and T6 stage a real clash: scorekeeping as resentment versus friendship as exchange.
T8 Stoic Realist names a concrete cost of T7's test to the lovely meetings.
Section E gives conditional branches tied to what the user values.
weaknesses: T7 Attachment Theorist proposes a two-week test the user has effectively already run.
Never asks about the friend's reasons, history or response to invitations (all turns).
Flat shared register and restatement openers across T4-T6 make the minds sound alike.

symptoms.observed: Two-week number not derived from user's facts; repeats observation user already made.
symptoms.evidence: wait two weeks without initiating contact

symptoms.observed: No turn asks why the friend might not initiate or whether they ever have.
symptoms.evidence: whether the friend is indifferent or simply passive

symptoms.observed: Attachment Theorist moves from communication-only to silent test with no stated cause.
symptoms.evidence: clear communication is the only way to determine

symptoms.observed: Cost and risk of actually raising it with the friend never weighed.
symptoms.evidence: It is important to express your desire for more balance

symptoms.observed: All three minds share one hedged advisory register.
symptoms.evidence: You should consider that you cannot force another person

findings.description: Debate attributes anxiety and insecurity to the user; the situation states neither.
Silent non-initiation test attributed to an Attached-based mind; the book emphasises direct effective communication and concerns romantic attachment.
Meditations dated 161; that is the start of Marcus's reign, the text is usually dated c. 170-180.

rubric_fit_notes: Matrix fits a relationship decision well. Uncertainty: whether the T7 test counts as redundant depends on reading 'if I stop texting, nothing happens' as observed fact rather than expectation; I read it as observed.
question_type_note: Read as a decision about whether to raise the imbalance, so speaking-up options, costs and observable conditions were weighed as written.
